NetBird releases before 0.74.4 pinned `golang.org/x/crypto` below 0.52.0 while the
SSH peer-access feature routes attacker-controlled SSH traffic through
`golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` handshake, authentication, session and channel handling
code.

The embedded SSH server is not enabled by default. It starts only when the local
`ServerSSHAllowed` setting is on *and* management enables SSH for the peer.
`client/internal/engine_ssh.go` then builds the server, binds the peer's NetBird
overlay address on the internal SSH port, and serves accepted connections through
`github.com/gliderlabs/ssh`, which calls `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.NewServerConn`.
Where it is enabled, the vulnerable parser and connection paths are reached
before shell, SFTP or port-forward authorization.

## Reachable advisories

`govulncheck` against `./client/ssh/...` at the v0.74.3 release commit reports
nine `golang.org/x/crypto` advisories fixed in 0.52.0. Four are reachable in the
server role:

| Advisory | CVE | Issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GO-2026-5013 | CVE-2026-46597 | AES-GCM packet decoder underflow, pre-authentication panic |
| GO-2026-5017 | CVE-2026-39830 | Server deadlock on unexpected client responses |
| GO-2026-5018 | CVE-2026-39829 | Pathological RSA/DSA parameters cause DoS |
| GO-2026-5020 | CVE-2026-39834 | Infinite loop on large channel writes |

Two are reachable in the client role, through `tryKnownHostsVerification` in
`client/ssh/client/client.go`, where a hostile SSH server is the attacker:

| Advisory | CVE | Issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GO-2026-5015 | CVE-2026-39835 | Panic during `CheckHostKey` / `Authenticate` |
| GO-2026-5021 | CVE-2026-42508 | `@revoked` status not enforced in `ssh/knownhosts` |

The remaining three need authentication features this server does not configure.
It registers no `PublicKeyHandler` and no certificate checker; authentication is
overlay source-IP validation plus optional JWT through a password handler:

| Advisory | CVE | Requires |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GO-2026-5014 | CVE-2026-39828 | SSH certificate authentication |
| GO-2026-5019 | CVE-2026-39831 | FIDO/U2F security-key authentication |
| GO-2026-5023 | CVE-2026-46595 | `VerifiedPublicKeyCallback` |

All nine are cleared by the same dependency bump, so the distinction does not
change the remediation.

## Impact

Denial of service against a peer running the SSH server. GO-2026-5013 is the
most serious: the panic occurs pre-authentication, inside `x/crypto`'s own
connection goroutines, so a single crafted connection takes down the whole
NetBird client daemon rather than only the SSH feature. Connectivity for that
peer is lost, not just SSH access to it.

Exposure is bounded. The SSH server must be enabled, the listener binds the
NetBird overlay address, and the connection validator rejects non-overlay source
addresses, so this is not reachable from outside the overlay. Within the
overlay, reach is limited to peers whose access-control policy permits the SSH
port.

## Fix

Fixed in 0.74.4. `golang.org/x/crypto` was raised to v0.54.0, along with
`golang.org/x/net` v0.56.0 and the Go 1.25.12 toolchain, in
[#6709](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/6709) on the `0.74.4-branch`
release branch; [#6727](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/6727) carried
the same change to `main`. After the bump `govulncheck` reports no remaining
reachable `x/crypto/ssh` advisories. Current releases carry v0.55.0.

Operators running a client older than 0.74.4 should upgrade. On any version,
disabling the SSH server removes the server-side exposure.

## Affected platforms

Desktop clients. The server-side exposure applies only where the SSH server has
been enabled; it is off by default, as `ServerSSHAllowed` defaults to false.

Android exposes the same setting and also defaults it to false, so an Android
peer is affected only where its user has deliberately enabled the SSH server.
The two client-role advisories do not apply on Android: its SSH client verifies
host keys against the peer key from the network map and never falls back to
`known_hosts`. iOS exposes neither the SSH server setting nor an SSH client.

## Credit

Reported by [@Faze-up](https://github.com/Faze-up).
